meta.title: Ch 14: Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 14 (Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring).

questions.q: Acquirer EPS Rs 20, target EPS Rs 8; target shareholders demand 1.5:1 exchange ratio. In the combined entity, the ratio is:
questions.why: A 1.5:1 ratio = 1.5 acquirer shares for each target share; the inverse (0.67) would be per acquirer share — the inversion is the trap; value ratio 1.5×20 = 30 vs target EPS 8 (P/E paid 3.75).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — ratio-direction inversion traps recur Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Read which way the fraction points: shares per share or share per shares.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: If merger synergies materialise only after 3 years (delayed), the acquirer should value them by:
o: Adding to year-1 cash flows and discounting 1 year
Discounting to year 0 through years 1-3 at project risk, with a haircut for realisation
questions.why: Realisation lag must be honoured: discount the full delay; assign higher risk (or probability weight) to promised synergies — the discount rate for synergies often above acquirer's cost of capital.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the delayed-synergy discounting is the trap variant AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A promise kept in year 4 is worth a year-4 number — discount it to today, and doubt it.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: An earn-out clause in an acquisition:
o: Defers part of consideration contingent on future performance
questions.why: Contingent consideration for performance/valuation gaps — shifts risk to sellers, addresses information asymmetry; Ind AS 103 measures at FV if liability-classified.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — structure-vocabulary for M&A deals Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: If you disagree about the future, pay for it when it arrives.

questions.q: A shareholder rights plan (poison pill) deters:
o: Hostile takeover by diluting the acquirer's stake if triggered
questions.why: Rights plan lets non-acquirer shareholders buy cheaply upon trigger — dilutes a creeping hostile bidder.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — defence-vocabulary recognition Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Make the raider's own army buy shares over his head.

questions.q: In an all-cash acquisition funded by debt, EPS accretion depends chiefly on:
o: After-tax cost of debt vs target's P/E (earnings yield) comparison
questions.why: Cash deal accretive if earnings yield of target (1/PE) > after-tax interest cost of the funding; the inverse → dilutive — the only real test in a cash deal.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the yield-vs-cost comparison is the entire cash-deal arithmetic AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Buy earnings cheaper than your money costs, and every EPS grows.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: Target's standalone value Rs 2,000 crore; synergy Rs 400 crore; acquirer pays Rs 2,300 crore. Premium to the acquirer's shareholders' wealth:
o: +100 −200? The target captures 300 of 400 synergy; acquirer shareholders' NPV = 400 − 300 = +100 crore
questions.why: Acquirer NPV = synergy − premium (2,300 − 2,000 = 300) = +100. The 'who captures the synergy' arithmetic — premium over target's standalone, not the offer size.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the split-of-pie calculation defines bid discipline AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Pay for the synergy you create minus what the auction makes you pay — the rest is the deal's worth.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: Target trades at P/E 5x; the cash comes from debt at 8% pre-tax (tax 25%). In the earnings-yield vs funding-cost test the deal is:
o: Cannot judge without P/E of acquirer
questions.why: Target earnings yield = 1/5 = 20.0%; funding cost after tax = 6.0%; yield above cost ⇒ accretion (ignoring synergies).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the yield-vs-cost test is the entire cash-merger MCQ genre Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Accretive if target earnings yield > after-tax cost of cash.

questions.why: Offer value = 50 × 1.50? 62.5 ⇒ ÷ 80 = 0.78 per target share — always 'shares of acquirer per share of target'.

questions.q: Target worth 600 standalone; synergy value 150; acquirer pays 700. The acquisition's net value creation to the ACQUIRER's shareholders is:
questions.why: Value to acquirer = synergy − premium paid = 150 − (700−600) = 50 to target holders? Careful: total pie grows 150; target keeps 100 as premium; acquirer nets +50 only if synergies are fully realised — the classic point: price discipline decides who gets the synergy.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the premium line is the acquirer's bid for the synergy; win = synergy left after premium Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Synergy is the pie that grows; the premium decides who eats it.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: Under SEBI SAST (as amended across notifications), acquiring shares/voting rights crossing 25% (or creeping beyond the permitted threshold) requires:
o: A public open offer to acquire 26% of the target's voting rights from all shareholders at a regulated price
questions.why: DOCUMENTED regime: crossing the acquisition threshold triggers a mandatory open offer sized to give everyone an exit at a price derived from the deal/ market benchmarks per the regulations — verify current threshold percentages and pricing formula against the notification in force for the attempt year.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — creeping in past the gate = open the door for all AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Sneak past 25% and the whole street gets the invitation.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: For tax benefits under sec 72A-type conditions on amalgamation (verify current Income-tax Act thresholds), the classic tests include:
o: Amalgamating company's shareholders holding 25%+ voting control continuing 3 years; assets/liabilities of the transferor carried over
questions.why: The scheme's accounting (Ind AS/AS pooling-of-interests) and tax definitions are independent — exam answers must state both books' tests separately; the pooling-of-interests accounting conditions (AS-14 / Schedule III practice) differ from the Income-tax conditions, and both need 'verify current law' flagging where percentages move.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — accounting tests and tax tests are twins, never identical AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: One merger, three rulebooks: corporate law, accounting, tax.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

questions.q: In a stressed-asset sale/winding-up, the correct payment order is:
o: Workmen' and secured creditors' claims as per the governing insolvency statute, then other claims per the priority ladder of that statute — verify current IBC waterfall order
Promoters last after all creditors, always
questions.why: The IBC (and its amendments and case law have shifted the exact ordering of workmen/taxes vs secured in some tranches) has a statutory waterfall; answer with the statute's ladder and cite that recent amendments have refined it — never recite a 'natural' order.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the statute holds the ladder; case law sometimes re-rungs it Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Who eats first in an insolvency is written in law, not in sympathy.
